title: Geometry - Lesson 6 Assessment: Reasoning and Proof Foundations
description: Show mastery of inductive and deductive reasoning, counterexamples, and statement-reason proof foundations.

questions.question: Which situation best shows deductive reasoning?
options: Measuring four drawings and guessing the next one has the same property
Using the theorem "vertical angles are congruent" to conclude two vertical angles are equal
Noticing that several squares have four equal sides
Drawing one trapezoid and making a general claim about all trapezoids
questions.explanation: Deductive reasoning uses an accepted theorem to support a conclusion.

questions.question: Conjecture: "All supplementary angles form a linear pair." Which counterexample disproves it?
options: Two adjacent angles that form a straight line
Two vertical angles that are both 90 degrees
A 60 degree angle and a 120 degree angle in separate diagrams
Two angles with measures 30 degrees and 50 degrees
questions.explanation: The 60 degree and 120 degree angles are supplementary but do not form a linear pair if they are not adjacent.

questions.question: Given: M is the midpoint of segment AB. Which statement follows by definition of midpoint?
questions.explanation: A midpoint divides a segment into two congruent parts, so AM = MB.

questions.question: A theorem can be used as a reason in a proof because it has already been proven.
questions.explanation: Theorems are proven results, so they are valid proof reasons.

questions.question: A conjecture is the same as a completed proof.
questions.explanation: A conjecture is an unproven statement. It may later be proven or disproven.

questions.question: In a two-column proof, the claim written on a line is the ______, and the support for that claim is the reason.
questions.explanation: A proof line contains a statement and a reason.

questions.question: If angles A and B are supplementary, then m∠A + m∠B = ______ degrees.
questions.explanation: Supplementary angles have measures that add to 180 degrees.

questions.question: Classify the reasoning as inductive or deductive: "ABCD is a parallelogram. Opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent. Therefore, AB is congruent to CD." Explain briefly.
questions.correctAnswer: Deductive reasoning, because it uses a known property of parallelograms to reach a specific conclusion about ABCD.
questions.explanation: The argument starts from an accepted property, so it is deductive.

questions.question: Give a counterexample to the conjecture: "Every quadrilateral has at least one pair of parallel sides."
questions.correctAnswer: A kite with no parallel sides is a counterexample because it is a quadrilateral but does not have a pair of parallel sides.
questions.explanation: One quadrilateral with no parallel sides is enough to disprove the conjecture.

questions.question: Complete this proof foundation: Given ∠1 and ∠2 form a linear pair. Statement: m∠1 + m∠2 = 180°. What is a valid reason?
questions.explanation: The Linear Pair Postulate says angles that form a linear pair are supplementary, so their measures add to 180 degrees.
